label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.2, 1003a33-b10: BEING_2 is said in many ways, but all in relation to one…
interpretation: Read as stated: being is said in many ways, but in relation to one nature and one principle and not homonymously, as 'healthy' is said of what preserves, produces, signifies or receives health; some things are called beings as substances, others as affections of substance, a way to substance, its destructions, privations, qualities, or what produces it. Not formalized. It supplies the 'pros hen' sense of DEF-BEING-ANALOGICAL; it does not say that being admits of more and less, nor that the primary sense is God (the primary here is substance).
